question.:question/problem: Find the value of $n$ that satisfies the equation ${625}^{n}={125}^{n-4}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
To solve this equation, we need both exponential terms to have a common base. To do this, we rewrite the equation using $625={5}^{4}$ and $125={5}^{3},$ as follows:

$$
{({5}^{4})}^{n}={({5}^{3})}^{n-4}
$$

Then, we apply the power rule of exponents. This gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{5}^{4n}={5}^{3(n-4)}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since both sides of the equation share the same base $(5)$, we equate the exponents and solve for $n:$

$$
\begin{aligned}4n & =3(n-4) \\ 4n & =3n-12 \\ n & =-12\end{aligned}
$$
